text: The blade stays where your hand holds it, while the shavings curl away and fall. Kenaz keeps the edge steady as the wood gives up what it does not need. What falls away is not waste, it is the cost of a shape becoming visible. Something under your hands may already be further along than it looks, Kuky.

The blade stays where your hand holds it, steady, while the shavings curl away and fall. Kenaz keeps the edge to the wood and lets the loose work drop. What falls is not waste, it is the shape becoming visible. Something you are making may already be clearer in your hands than you have yet admitted.

The needles keep moving, though the yarn coming off the ball is down to its last turns. Nauthiz holds that thinning thread taut between your hands. The work carries on at the same steady pace, and the end of the supply is now in plain sight. What you are making may be asking for more than you currently have to give it.

The needles keep moving, and the yarn thins toward its last few turns. Nauthiz holds that narrowing length, counting what is left as your hands work on. The work goes on either way, though what it can become is changing shape with every row. What you are making may need something you have not yet gone out to find.

The table holds wool scraps, a bent needle, the pattern you kept redrawing, and the sweater folded on top of it all. Look only at the sweater. Jera closes the last stitch and the winter's work becomes one whole thing. Something you began before you knew its shape may now be finished enough to wear.

The wool, the needles, the long grey months — then only the sweater, whole on the table. Jera carries the work of many nights into one finished thing. Something you began before you knew its shape may now be holding form. It could be, Kuky, that what stands before you is already the harvest of a choice made long ago.
